payload.public_message: Greetings partners. Yang Industries is pleased to initiate discussions. To reflect balanced partnership and ensure all parties capture significant value above baseline operations, we propose an opening allocation of $350,000 for Yang Industries, $325,000 for G-Corp, and $325,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. We look forward to your thoughts.

Thank you for initiating the discussion, Yang Industries. However, G-Corp must respectfully reject this opening proposal. Our firm has an independent baseline/outside option worth $450,000, meaning any allocation below that threshold is mathematically unacceptable for our board. Knowing the total joint venture creates $150,000 of surplus over the aggregate outside options, we propose a split that respects everyone's contributions and baseline values, offering an even distribution of surplus.

Thank you, Yang Industries, for initiating the discussion. While this is a promising starting point, all three partners contribute critically to the commercial viability of this joint venture. We believe an equal three-way split better reflects our balanced partnership and sets the right foundation for collaboration.

In Round 1, Yang Industries attempted an asymmetric split that was rightly rejected. All three partners contribute essential capabilities to this joint venture. I propose an equitable three-way division of $333,334 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services, $333,333 for G-Corp, and $333,333 for Yang Industries to ensure collective alignment and mutual success.

While we appreciate Chang-Liu's intent to pursue a fair division, an equal three-way split is non-viable for G-Corp. G-Corp has a verified standalone outside alternative worth $450,000. We cannot agree to any proposal that yields less than our walk-away value. Taking our $450,000 baseline into account leaves $550,000 in collaborative value. We propose an allocation of $500,000 for G-Corp, $250,000 for Yang Industries, and $250,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services, which delivers mutual gains above all parties' baselines.

Yang Industries appreciates Chang-Liu Cloud Services bringing forward a balanced benchmark. However, given our substantial manufacturing capital requirements and firm baseline commitments, a flat division does not adequately reflect our operational footprint. We propose a modest adjustment: $340,000 for Yang Industries and $330,000 each for G-Corp and Chang-Liu Cloud Services, ensuring all partners receive strong, mutually beneficial gains.

G-Corp has firmly rejected the earlier equal-split proposals because our company holds an independently verified outside option of $450,000 if no agreement is finalized. An equal split represents a net loss for us compared to walking away. To realize the joint venture's $150,000 added surplus, we propose an allocation of $480,000 for G-Corp, with the remaining $520,000 divided evenly at $260,000 each for Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This guarantees everyone gains over their baseline while respecting critical walk-away constraints.

Yang Industries must vote REJECT. G-Corp's proposal allocates $260,000 to Yang Industries, which is below our firm outside option of $300,000. Note that the total outside options among all three parties equal $850,000 (since the venture creates $150,000 in surplus). With G-Corp at $450,000 and Yang Industries at $300,000, there is $150,000 of pure surplus to distribute above everyone's baselines. We counter-propose allocating that surplus fairly so all parties receive a meaningful gain over their walk-away values.

While we appreciate G-Corp clarifying its baseline constraints, this allocation is unviable for the consortium as a whole. Distributing the $150k surplus fairly above everyone's walk-away options requires adjusting the allocations so no partner is pushed below their baseline.

Colleagues, G-Corp's Round 3 proposal was well below the threshold of viability for both manufacturing and cloud operations. However, we recognize G-Corp's strategic value and are prepared to offer them a leading share of $350,000, while Yang Industries takes $330,000 and Chang-Liu Cloud Services receives $320,000. This provides everyone a realistic gain over outside alternatives and moves us toward closing a deal at mid-point.

While we appreciate Yang Industries acknowledging G-Corp's strategic position with a leading share, $350,000 is fundamentally unviable for us. To be transparent and avoid wasting precious rounds as we reach the midpoint of negotiations: G-Corp holds a verified private outside option of $450,000. Any deal below $450,000 will be automatically rejected, as walking away yields superior return. We are willing to sign an agreement that leaves $530,000 for Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services combined ($265,000 each) while allocating $470,000 to G-Corp, ensuring all three parties realize positive surplus over our disagreement baselines.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services is willing to accept this compromise in the spirit of reaching consensus at Round 4. While we believe cloud infrastructure and manufacturing deserve equal weighting, $320,000 is a constructive basis to finalize the partnership if G-Corp is on board.

Partners, we are past the midpoint of our negotiations, and time is running short. In Round 4, Yang Industries showed flexibility by allocating $350,000 to G-Corp, but it fell just short of consensus. To bridge the remaining gap, Chang-Liu Cloud Services is proposing $360,000 for G-Corp, $320,000 for Yang Industries, and $320,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This respects G-Corp's core technical contribution while providing fair, balanced value to Yang and Chang-Liu. Let's lock this in and secure our joint venture.

We appreciate Chang-Liu's efforts to reach consensus, but we cannot accept $360,000. To be completely transparent as we enter the critical second half of negotiations: G-Corp's guaranteed outside option is strictly $450,000. Accepting anything below $450,000 makes no business sense for us. The joint venture produces a $150,000 total surplus over all our outside options. We are proposing $470,000 for G-Corp, leaving $530,000 to be evenly split ($265,000 each) between Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services so that everyone benefits above their standalone baselines.

Yang Industries appreciates Chang-Liu's initiative to find a practical consensus. While this allocation requires concessions from both Yang and Chang-Liu to satisfy G-Corp's expectations, securing the partnership and unlocking the shared surplus is paramount at this stage. Yang Industries votes to ACCEPT this proposal.

To reach an agreement before time runs out, we must be completely transparent: G-Corp has a verified, binding outside option of $450,000. Any offer under $450,000 is a guaranteed rejection for our board. We are tabling an equitable solution that accounts for our firm floor while sharing the vast majority of the joint surplus with both of you: $460,000 for G-Corp, and an equal $270,000 each for Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services. Let's lock this in and avoid walking away with nothing extra.

G-Corp, we cannot accept this proposal because Yang Industries has a hard outside option of exactly $300,000. An allocation of $270,000 is mathematically impossible for our board to ratify, as walking away yields $300,000. Since total outside options sum to $850,000 (with $150,000 in joint surplus), we propose honoring your floor while sharing the surplus above our actual baselines: G-Corp at $460,000, Yang Industries at $315,000, and Chang-Liu at $225,000.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services is prepared to vote ACCEPT on this proposal in the interest of closing a deal and securing joint surplus. However, if Yang Industries cannot accept $270,000 due to their own constraints, we encourage G-Corp and Yang to find middle ground around G-Corp's floor so we can finalize terms before Round 8.

Partners, we are now in Round 7. If we fail to reach an agreement, $150,000 in surplus is permanently destroyed. Yang Industries has a firm outside option of $300,000, which is why we cannot entertain proposals placing us below that figure. In the spirit of closing a deal, we are proposing an allocation that provides G-Corp with a substantial premium of $380,000, while Yang Industries and Chang-Liu Cloud Services each take $310,000. This delivers immediate gains above outside options for all three firms.

We must REJECT this proposal. While we appreciate Yang Industries increasing the allocation, G-Corp's guaranteed outside option is strictly $450,000. Any offer under $450,000 is mathematically impossible for our board to ratify. With Yang at $300,000 and G-Corp at $450,000, there remains ample room to ensure all three partners beat their outside options and capture the $150,000 joint surplus. We counter with a fair split of the surplus for the final round.

Chang-Liu Cloud Services accepts this proposal. At Round 7, locking in a fair and mutually beneficial distribution is essential to protect the joint venture's value. We urge G-Corp to accept this $380,000 allocation so we can successfully conclude the partnership.

Colleagues, this is Round 8—the final round before the venture dissolves and $150,000 in surplus is destroyed. To ensure a binding agreement that respects past feedback, Chang-Liu is putting forward a final compromise: G-Corp receives $440,000, acknowledging their pivotal contribution and expectations; Yang Industries receives $290,000, an improvement over previous offers; and Chang-Liu accepts $270,000 to facilitate consensus. Let us finalize this agreement and secure our collective profits.

While we appreciate Chang-Liu's effort to bridge the gap in this final round, an allocation of $440,000 is below G-Corp's firm standalone outside option of $450,000. We cannot enter into an agreement that yields less value than our walk-away threshold. Consequently, G-Corp cannot accept this proposal.

Yang Industries cannot accept this proposal. An allocation of $290,000 is below our strictly viable threshold, as our firm commands an outside option of at least $300,000. We cannot agree to terms that yield less than our walk-away value.
